title: Responsiveness-tiered dampening and multi-window autoscaler
author: Maya Sutherland
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets currently oscillate between reactive scaling and conservative stability for multi-tenant workloads. Small transient spikes cause unnecessary provisioning churn while long-term trend shifts are slow to converge. This PR introduces a multi-window autoscaler that balances short-term responsiveness with long-term stability via a dampening mechanism and per-tenant soft admission limits. Goals: 1) Reduce oscillation from microbursts while preserving fast recovery for genuine sustained demand; 2) Provide deterministic per-tenant throughput guarantees (soft limits) with graceful degradation under contention; 3) Surface new telemetry to evaluate headroom, utilization quantiles, and damping efficacy. Summary of changes: - New component src/autoscaler/multi_window_autoscaler.go: implements two-window controller (short window = 10s-30s, long window = 5m-15m) with configurable weighting and exponential dampening on scale decisions. - Admission refactor src/scheduler/soft_admission.go: introduces per-tenant soft-limits and a soft-deny path that enqueues requests into a priority-deferrable queue rather than hard rejecting. - Burst token bucket enhancer src/autoscaler/burst_banker.go: adds proportional decay to burst credits and a safety floor to prevent negative headroom. - Telemetry additions metrics/telemetry/tenant_util_quantiles.promql and metrics/telemetry/headroom_histogram.promql: emit p50/p90/p99 tenant utilization and headroom distribution, plus dampening events counter. - Policy config configs/dedicated/throughput_policy_v2.yaml: expose damping coefficients, multi-window parameters, and soft-limit tiers (gold/silver/bronze). - E2E tests tests/e2e/responsiveness_autoscale_test.py: synthetic workload harness that asserts stability under periodic microbursts and responsiveness on sustained ramps. - Docs docs/design/multi-window-autoscaler.md: design rationale, tuning guidance, and runbook entries for incident analysis. Backwards compatibility: The autoscaler is opt-in via the throughput_policy_v2.yaml feature flag; default behavior remains the existing single-window scaler until rollout is enabled for a fleet. Checklist: - [x] Implementation compiles and unit tests added - [x] E2E harness validates key scenarios (burst, ramp up/ramp down) - [x] Telemetry dashboards prototyped and prometheus queries added - [x] Feature flag gated for gradual rollout - [x] Docs and runbook updated for on-call teams Performance notes: In internal canary across two small fleets we observed a ~28% reduction in spurious scale-up events driven by short microbursts and a ~12% improvement in 99th percentile requester latency during burst windows due to smarter soft-admit behavior. Related: builds on ideas from ENG-531 (headroom observability) and ties into SUP-4521 (customer incident where oscillation caused cost spikes). Tuning knobs (high level): - short_window_seconds: responsiveness to immediate load - long_window_seconds: trend smoothing - dampening_alpha: exponential decay factor applied to successive scale decisions - soft_limit_tiers: per-tenant throughput floors and burst ceilings Rollout plan: 1) Enable on non-production dedicated fleets behind feature flag; 2) Monitor headroom/dampening events for 2 weeks; 3) Canary on low-traffic production fleets; 4) Gradual rollout with telemetry gating.
commits: feat(autoscaler): add multi-window autoscaler controller implementation
refactor(scheduler): introduce soft admission APIs and priority deferrable queue
feat(telemetry): expose tenant utilization quantiles and dampening counters
chore(config): add throughput_policy_v2.yaml and feature flag
test(e2e): add responsiveness_autoscale_test with microburst scenarios
docs: design write-up and runbook for multi-window autoscaler
fix(burst): enforce non-negative burst credit floor and proportional decay math
ci: expand unit test matrix and flaky e2e retry logic
review_comments: Arjun Patel: Can you explain why we chose exponential dampening instead of simple cooldown windows? I'm worried about long tails if alpha isn't tuned.

Maya Sutherland: Reply: Exponential dampening lets us reduce the effective weight of repeated scale actions without rigid cooldowns; it composes with the long window trend smoother to ensure we recover from real sustained demand. Added tuning guidance in the docs and a safety max-scale cap to avoid long-tail over-throttling.
Lina Gómez: Tests look good but I want to see an assertion for soft-admit fairness across tiers (gold shouldn't be starved by bursty bronze).
Maya Sutherland: Reply: Added fairness assertion to e2e harness and a proportional backfill path so gold tenants maintain minimum throughput when contention is present.
Tom Brewer: CI reported a flaky e2e on first run (race in queue draining). Please add a drain-wait and re-run.
Maya Sutherland: Reply: Fixed queue drain race and added deterministic seed in the synthetic generator. Reran CI and green.
release_notes: Introduce an opt-in multi-window autoscaler for Dedicated fleets that reduces oscillation and improves responsiveness. Adds per-tenant soft admission limits, new telemetry for utilization quantiles and headroom, and configuration knobs for dampening and window sizes. Feature gated and safe to roll out gradually.
